title: Hydraulic and Pneumatic Systems
summary: How liquids and gases transfer force, Pascal's principle, pressure, mechanical advantage of hydraulic systems, and everyday uses of hydraulics and pneumatics.

items: **Hydraulic** systems use a **liquid** (usually oil or water) to transfer force.
**Pneumatic** systems use a **gas** (usually compressed air) to transfer force.

rows: Liquids cannot be compressed, so movement is precise and firm
Gases can be compressed, so movement is springy and cushioned
Car brakes, car jacks, excavators, barber chairs, dump trucks
Bus doors, dentist's drills, jackhammers, tyre inflation, air brakes on trucks

notes.caption: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa): 1 Pa = 1 N/m². In syringe calculations we often use N/cm².

notes.title: Calculating pressure
notes.problem: A force of 100 N acts on a piston with an area of 0,002 m². Calculate the pressure.

notes.label: Pascal's principle
notes.text: Pressure applied to a liquid in a closed system is transmitted **equally in all directions** throughout the liquid.

In a hydraulic system with two cylinders (pistons) of different sizes, the **pressure is the same** in both. A small force on a **small** piston creates a pressure that pushes on a **large** piston with a **larger** force. This is how a hydraulic jack lets one person lift a car.

notes.title: A hydraulic jack
notes.problem: The small piston of a hydraulic jack has an area of 2 cm² and the large piston an area of 50 cm². A force of 100 N is applied to the small piston. (a) What is the pressure in the liquid? (b) What force does the large piston exert? (c) What is the mechanical advantage?

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: There is a trade-off: the large piston pushes with more force but moves a **shorter distance**. If the small piston moves 25 cm, the large piston in the example moves only 1 cm.

In the classroom, **syringes** connected by plastic tubing model hydraulic systems. Filled with water they act hydraulically (firm, precise); filled with air they act pneumatically (springy). They can be used to operate the arm of a model crane, a robotic hand or a drawbridge.

Use a smaller input syringe and a larger output syringe to increase force.

questions.memo:
✓ Hydraulics: large force / precise, firm movement (1)
✓ Pneumatics: clean / fast / cushioned movement / air is free (1)

questions.prompt: In a hydraulic jack, the large piston exerts a much bigger force than the effort. What is the disadvantage?
questions.memo:
✓ The large piston moves a much shorter distance (1)
✓ so the small piston must be pumped many times / over a long distance (1)
